statement.zh-TW: 晴川花坊上個月替一家餐廳布置開幕花藝並賒帳，這個月收到了這筆 {{money:vars.amount}} 的款項。這個月的損益表可以把這 {{money:vars.amount}} 列為營業收入。
statement.en: Last month Clearwater Florist decorated a restaurant opening on credit; this month it collects the {{money:vars.amount}} it was owed. This month’s income statement can show the {{money:vars.amount}} as revenue.

feedbackTrue.zh-TW: 錢確實是這個月進來的，這點沒錯。不過這筆生意的收入上個月布置完成時就已經認列了；這個月收款只是把應收帳款換成現金，如果再列一次收入，同一筆生意就算了兩次。
feedbackTrue.en: The money did arrive this month, that much is right. But the revenue on this job was recognised last month when the decorating was done; collecting it this month merely turns a receivable into cash, and showing it as revenue again would count the same job twice.

feedbackFalse.zh-TW: 答對了。收入在賺到的那個月認列，收款那個月只動現金和應收帳款。
feedbackFalse.en: That is right. Revenue is recognised in the month it is earned; the month of collection only moves cash and receivables.

explanation.zh-TW: {{term:tm_05t9wphy}}下，收入跟著「賺到」走，不跟著「收到」走。賒銷那個月：收入與{{term:tm_r7x2c9fa}}增加；收款這個月：現金增加、應收帳款減少，收入不再變動。
explanation.en: Under the {{term:tm_05t9wphy}}, revenue follows earning, not receiving. In the month of the credit sale, revenue and {{term:tm_r7x2c9fa}} rise; in the month of collection, cash rises and receivables fall, and revenue does not move again.
